battle.name: 隋馮盎平僚人叛亂
battle.brief: 仁壽元年（601）嶺南僚人山寨起兵，隋文帝命廣州總管馮盎為行軍總管，率官軍自廣州西進，會同冼夫人所遣山地兵力，攻破循州一帶寨城。攻城時隋軍將投石機架於高處，拋石毀牆破堞，為步卒登寨開路。本役史載簡略，投石機數目與所毀工事形制皆無可確證。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 仁壽元年（601）嶺南用兵，參戰方大致分為兩陣營。其一是隋朝中央與嶺南各郡縣的官軍體系：指揮中樞在京城，仁壽元年隋文帝楊堅仍在位，詔以鎮守廣州的馮盎為行軍總管，總攝平叛諸軍；廣州、循州、交州一線的守令、城戍卒與鄉兵歸馮盎調度，本地郡兵之外，隋廷未自北方調大軍南下，可見此役在朝廷的定位是局部平叛而非全面戰爭。與官軍並肩作戰的，是高涼冼氏所率俚族兵眾：冼夫人以譙國夫人號令一方，其孫陳魂率領熟悉谿谷、識路識水的山地隊伍，參與攻寨與斷糧；隋廷對這支力量一向以「以夷制夷」的方式加以倚重。反方是嶺南山區的僚人（史籍亦作獠、俚）起兵勢力，並未建立政權名號，也沒有推舉共主，起事者以山寨為堡壘，以搶掠、斷道、拒官軍為主要手段，呈現多家分寨、各自為戰的格局，兵眾與糧秣主要靠劫掠內地村邑與山寨屯積取得。就雙方實力對比而言，官軍在兵員、器械、糧道與後方補給上佔優，起兵方則在地利、熟悉地形與前線耳目上佔優，這一攻守結構從一開始便決定了本役的走向。
countriesEn: The fighting in Lingnan in 601 pits two camps against each other. On the Sui side stands the army of the imperial court together with the commanderies and counties of Lingnan: the centre of command lies at the capital, and in the first year of Renshou Emperor Wen of Sui Yang Jian was still reigning, so the edict named Feng Ang, who governed Guangzhou, as overall commander of the pacifying force. The magistrates, the city garrisons and the local militia of Guangzhou, Xunzhou and Jiaozhou were all placed under his orders, and no major army was brought down from the north, which shows how the court regarded the affair, as a local pacification rather than a general war. Fighting shoulder to shoulder with the regular troops were the indigenous companies of the Xian clan of Gaoliang: Lady Xian, addressed as the Lady of the Guo, held authority over a network of clans, and her grandson Chen Hun led mountain troops who knew every ravine, every path and every ford, taking part in the assault on the forts and in the cutting of the rebels' supplies. The court always relied on this force in the deliberate manner of using the local chiefs to control the local people. On the other side stand the insurgents, the Liao of the Lingnan mountains, whose records also write the name as Liao or Li. They formed no state, proclaimed no common ruler and possessed no unified command. Each fortified village was its own stronghold; the rebels relied on raiding, on cutting the roads and on holding out in the hills, and their men and grain came chiefly from what they could seize in the lowland villages and from what they had stored in the mountains. As for the balance of strength, the Sui field army held the advantage in numbers, in equipment, in supply lines and in the support of a rear base, while the insurgents held the advantage in terrain, in local knowledge and in early warning of the enemy's movements. That structure of attack and defence decided the course of the campaign from the outset.
people: 本役記錄中唯一有名可考的主帥是馮盎，字孟希，渤海郡高唐人。其父馮君恬仕北齊為太常卿，馮盎少時出入北周宮掖，開皇初與父奔陳，陳亡復歸隋，自儀同起步。開皇十年（590）番禺人王仲宣起兵逐盎、據廣州時，他靠高涼冼氏遣孫陳魂率俚兵接應而復位，此後總鎮廣州，成為隋廷在嶺南倚重的長將。仁壽元年僚人起事時，馮盎已年逾七十，是隋廷最能熟悉南疆的將帥，故詔書仍以之行軍總管，軍中大事必與之議。冼夫人是第二次被朝廷倚重的南方首領：開皇十年她曾遣孫率兵援馮盎、誅王仲宣，至此役又以年老之身遣部屬助隋討平嶺西山地起兵，隋廷因而加封其族，譙國夫人的號召力成為此役能迅速收束的關鍵。陳魂承祖輩兵威，領俚兵擔任攻寨先鋒，其弟陳坦與族中諸首領亦各率部眾隨行。山寨方面，各寨首領姓名多不見於傳記，僅知起事首領曾受陳朝舊部游說，以「拒官軍、護山寨」為號召。隋文帝在後方掌握發兵、發糧與賞罰之權，其晚年對南方用兵仍以「不動眾、不大舉」為原則，這一取向自上而下影響了本役的戰法。
peopleEn: The only commander named in the sources for this campaign is Feng Ang, courtesy name Mengxi, a native of Gaotang in Bohai commandery. His father Feng Juntian had served the Northern Qi as Grand Master of Ceremonies, and the younger Feng Ang moved in the palace of the Northern Zhou; at the beginning of the Kaihuang era he fled to the Chen together with his father, and after the fall of Chen he returned to the Sui and rose from the rank of yitong. In the tenth year of Kaihuang, 590, when the Panyu man Wang Zhongxuan rebelled, drove him out and seized Guangzhou, Feng Ang was restored to his post only because Lady Xian of Gaoliang sent her grandson Chen Hun with tribal troops to his support; from then on he governed Guangzhou and became the long-serving commander on whom the Sui court relied in the far south. When the Liao rising broke out in the first year of Renshou, Feng Ang was already over seventy, and he was the Sui general who knew the southern frontier best, so the edict named him commander in chief once more and all major decisions in the field were discussed with him. Lady Xian was the southern chief the court relied on for the second time: having sent her grandson with troops to support Feng Ang and punish Wang Zhongxuan in 590, in old age she once more dispatched her people to help the Sui put down the rising in the western hills, and the court rewarded her clan accordingly, her authority being the decisive reason why the campaign could be closed quickly. Chen Hun, inheriting the armed prestige of his family, led the tribal vanguard in the assault on the forts, and his brother Chen Tan and other clan chiefs followed with their own contingents. The names of the insurgent village chiefs are not preserved; all that is known is that they had been won over by survivors of the Chen court, whose slogan was to resist the court troops and to protect the mountain settlements. Emperor Wen held the levers of dispatch, of supply and of reward at the capital. In his late years he still followed the principle of sparing the people and avoiding a great expedition in the south, and that choice shaped the conduct of this campaign from above.
kits: 本役的器械主幹是投石機（onager）。其原理是以絞盤與配重把蓄力轉成投臂的角速度，末端的拋臂兜住石彈或陶罐，一放即出，射程可達二百步以上，是隋唐攻城戰中最直接有效的破壞器械。隋軍在嶺南山地攻寨，寨牆多以夯土、竹木與石塊混築，依山就勢，形制不統一，投石機的價值正在於不必依賴大型雲梯與巢車即可在短距離內摧毀牆體與屋頂，逼守軍暴露，再由步卒循缺口登寨。投石機之外，隋軍攻城常備巢車、飛樓、雲梯與撞車：撞車用以撞毀寨門，巢車與飛樓供兵居高臨下射擊與投擲火罐，雲梯則供步卒直攀牆頭。山地行軍還倚重刀、矛、弓箭與少量甲騎，但嶺南雨濕多霧，道路崎嶇，隋軍主力仍以步兵為主，騎兵主要用於山口封鎖與追擊。守寨一方沒有同等攻城器械，只能倚靠寨牆、壕溝、滾木礌石與高處投石反制，弓弩密集射擊使攻方器械操作手傷亡慘重。糧秣方面，隋軍由廣州倉儲出發，沿北江水路與嶺南驛道分批轉運，俚兵熟悉山地小徑，可以就近取食自給，減少了官軍長距離補給的負擔；兵器維修、火藥與石彈備料亦隨軍裝載。戰後隋廷在所平山寨改置官鎮、編置屯戍，把原本零散的器械消耗轉為常設的守備需求。
kitsEn: The instrument at the centre of this campaign was the onager, the traction trebuchet. Its principle is to convert the force stored by a winch and counterweight into the angular speed of a throwing beam, whose sling or bucket carries a stone or a clay jar and is released to fly over a range of more than two hundred paces, making it the most direct and effective destructive machine in the siege warfare of the Sui and the Tang. Attacking the mountain villages of Lingnan, the Sui found their walls built of rammed earth, bamboo, timber and stone rubble, laid out to follow the terrain and of no uniform plan. The value of the onager lay precisely in the fact that it could break a wall or a roof at short range without recourse to a great siege tower or scaling ladder, exposing the defenders so that infantry could climb through the breach. Beside the onager the Sui besiegers brought nest-ladders, flying towers, scaling ladders and battering rams: the ram for the gate, the tower and the flying platform for shooting down and for hurling fire-pots, the scaling ladders for the wall-head. On the march the army relied on sabres, spears, bows and a small number of armoured riders, but the damp, misty and broken roads of Lingnan kept infantry as the backbone, with the cavalry used chiefly to seal the passes and to pursue. The defenders had no siege machinery of their own and could only rely on walls, ditches, rolling logs and stones, and on missiles and stones dropped from the heights, whose volleys of arrows made the losses among the machine crews severe. As for supply, the Sui drew from the magazines of Guangzhou and moved the grain in batches by the Beijiang waterway and along the post roads of the south, while the tribal troops, familiar with the mountain tracks, fed themselves from the country they passed through and lightened the burden of the regular army's long haul; the repair of weapons, the powder and the ammunition stone all travelled with the column. After the victory the court set up official posts and registered garrisons in the pacified villages, converting what had been a scattered expenditure of machines into a standing requirement of defence.
tactics: 隋軍的戰法以「穩進、設圍、斷糧、攻心」四步為主。第一步穩進：行軍不求速，馮盎先以廣州為基地整備器械糧秣，再以小股先鋒沿北江支流與山徑西進，抵循州境內先立營柵、築壘自固，不在無險之地倉促接戰。第二步設圍：對起事山寨，隋軍分為數路，各據山口要道，環繞成圍，但不作四面強攻。第三步斷糧：切斷山寨與山下村邑的往來，使守寨者不能獲得鹽、米與鐵器，寨中糧盡自有潰散。第四步攻心：隋軍一面以官軍旗鼓示以正兵，一面由俚兵為嚮導，避開正路，潛行谿谷，從後方襲其心腹寨，攻守之勢因此逆轉。攻城時，投石機列於隋軍後列稍遠處的高地，發射石彈與陶罐，集中打擊寨牆、寨門上方守兵密集處與村寨屋頂，迫守軍退避；撞車隨之前推，撞開寨門，雲梯兵趁缺口攀緣而上，步卒隨之湧入寨內。寨破之後，隋軍並不屠戮寨眾，多就地招撫，以俚族首領仍舊牧其眾、授以官職的方式收編，殘部或散入深山，或隨降眾安置於平地。安置之後，隋廷設巡檢、置屯兵，把新平之地併入郡縣編戶與羈縻首領並存的體制，使「以夷制夷」成為常態，兵事轉為民政，同時在山口要害留戍卒以防再叛。
tacticsEn: The Sui method of fighting followed four steps: advance securely, encircle, cut the supplies, and break the will of the enemy. First, the secure advance: the column did not hurry. Feng Ang used Guangzhou as a base to prepare the machines and the grain, then sent a small vanguard west along the tributaries of the Beijiang and along the mountain paths, and on reaching the territory of Xunzhou he first raised camp fences and built a stockade to secure himself, refusing a premature engagement on ground that offered no natural advantage. Second, the encirclement: against the insurgent villages the Sui troops were divided into several columns, each holding a pass or a road and forming a ring around the settlement, but they did not press on all sides at once. Third, the cutting of supplies: patrols severed the traffic between the villages and the plain below, so that the defenders could no longer obtain salt, rice or iron, and hunger alone would empty the forts. Fourth, the attack on the will: the Sui displayed their banners and drums on the front, while tribal guides, moving silently through the ravines and avoiding the main roads, struck at the heart of the rebel position from behind, and the balance of the assault was reversed. At the walls the onagers were set up on higher ground a short distance behind the Sui line, hurling stones and clay jars at the walls, at the places above the gates where the defenders crowded together, and at the roofs of the village, forcing the garrisons to take cover; the rams were then pushed forward to burst the gates, the scaling ladders went up through the breach, and the infantry poured in after them. When a fort had fallen, the Sui did not slaughter the village: many were taken in and settled on the spot, the tribal chiefs keeping their people and receiving official rank, while the remnants either scattered into the deep mountains or were resettled on the plains. The pacified areas were then provided with patrols and garrison troops, and the newly taken ground was absorbed into a system in which registered commanderies and counties stood alongside recognised native chiefs, so that using the local people to control the local people became the norm; military affairs turned into civil administration, and troops were left at the passes to forestall a new rising.
data: 可以確定的數字不多，須逐一標明其確定程度。時間：起事與平叛都在仁壽元年（601）之內，隋文帝崩於同年十一月，平定當在此之前，隋朝其後才進入大業年號。人物年齡：馮盎在開皇十年（590）已任廣州總管，至此役時年逾七十，其卒年與享年各書記載有出入，姑從「開皇年間已在中年任事、仁壽年間為老將」推斷。距離：廣州至循州（今廣東雲浮、羅定一帶）陸路約四百里，山路迂曲，實際行程當更長；循州至交州方向另約數百里，嶺南地廣，一支偏師若單獨深入極易斷援。兵員：隋書與相關類書對此役只作數語記載，未留下可用的兵數、斬獲數與糧秣數，故本篇不列任何編制數字；可以說的是，隋廷未為此役自北方調大軍，兵力當以廣州、循州、交州本地郡兵、戍卒與俚族兵力為主，規模屬局部平叛。器械：投石機的數目無記載；依同代攻城慣例，投石機與撞車、雲梯配合使用，器械操作通常由專門的拋車兵或隨軍工匠擔任，攻城階段傷亡多集中於此。交通與補給：主要依北江水路與嶺南驛道，嶺南多雨、夏季炎熱，糧秣易腐，運輸季節直接影響進攻時機。水文：北江汛期水量豐，舟楫可深入支流，但山洪與潮汐使近山路段的陸運風險加高。氣候：嶺南夏無酷暑而濕熱多雨，雲霧多，能見度低，弓弩與投石的精度都受影響，故攻城多在秋冬乾季施行。以上為有根據可述者，確切數字則付闕如。
dataEn: Few figures are certain, and each must be qualified. Timing: both the rising and its suppression fall within the first year of Renshou, 601; Emperor Wen died in the eleventh month of that year, so the victory was won before his death, and only afterwards did the Sui enter the Daye era. Age: Feng Ang was already governor of Guangzhou in the tenth year of Kaihuang, 590, so in 601 he was over seventy; the sources disagree about his year of death and his age, and the safe inference is only that he was a middle-aged officer under the Kaihuang and an old general by the Renshou. Distances: roughly four hundred li by road from Guangzhou to Xunzhou, the modern Yunfu and Luoding area of Guangdong, and considerably more once the winding mountain roads are counted; several hundred li more in the direction of Jiaozhou. Lingnan is a vast region, and a detached column marching deep by itself ran the risk of being cut off. Troop numbers: the History of Sui and the related encyclopaedias condense this campaign into a few phrases and leave no usable figures for the strength of the army, for the losses inflicted or for the quantity of grain, so no numbers of this kind are given here; what can be said is that the court brought no major army from the north for this business, so the force must have consisted chiefly of the local commandery troops, the garrisons and the tribal companies of Guangzhou, Xunzhou and Jiaozhou, and was therefore a local pacification. Machines: no number of onagers is recorded; by the siege practice of the time the onager worked together with the ram and the scaling ladders, and the machines were worked by specialists, the crews of the trebuchets or the engineer craftsmen who travelled with the army, and it was among them that the losses of the assault fell most heavily. Lines of movement and supply: the Beijiang waterway and the post roads of the south; Lingnan is rainy and hot in the summer and the grain spoils easily, so the season of transport governed the timing of the attack. Hydrology: the Beijiang carries a great volume in the flood season and boats can reach far up the tributaries, but flash floods and the tidal rise made the last stretch of the road more risky. Climate: Lingnan is not brutally hot, but it is humid, rainy and foggy, and the low visibility reduced the accuracy of both the arrows and the stones, which is why sieges were generally undertaken in the dry months of autumn and winter. Such are the statements that can be supported; the exact figures simply are not recorded.
cause: 這場衝突的直接起因，是隋朝在嶺南的編戶與羈縻體制跟當地山地社會之間的矛盾。開皇九年（589）隋平陳後，嶺南歸入新朝，隋廷在廣州、循州、羅州、交州一線設郡置縣，同時沿用陳朝以來的做法，讓俚族首領出任州刺史、縣令甚至封侯，藉其治理山寨、徵發貢賦。問題在於，郡縣官員與俚族首領彼此不信任：郡吏為求政績與私利，常加派徭役、索取珍貨、沒收山寨所產兵器，俚族首領則利用其熟悉山道與村落的便利，把中央政令截留於峒壑，兩邊互相告訐，久而久之積怨於山中。外部刺激也起了作用：陳朝覆亡十餘年，陳氏舊臣與遺民散入嶺南山區，以「復陳」「拒隋」相號召，並向寨落陳說官軍不過暫來，誘使起事。仁壽元年前後，隋文帝晚年多病，京城謠言並起，遠近傳聞隋祚將盡，山區的寨落把這類說法視為可乘之機；加之隋廷在嶺南的徵發與營造工事逐漸加劇，役事與攤派落在最無力抗拒的村落身上，遂使怨氣匯聚成旗。開皇十年番禺王仲宣之亂已顯示嶺南不服的暗火未曾熄滅，十一年間的太平只是壓制，並未解決結構性的病根。於是仁壽元年之際，山區數寨先後響應，隋廷不能再以羈縻敷衍，必須出兵，而最熟悉南疆的廣州總管馮盎，遂成為唯一可信賴的統帥。
causeEn: The immediate cause of this conflict lay in the tension between the Sui system of registered households and native chieftaincies in Lingnan and the mountain communities of the region. After the Sui destroyed the Chen in 589, Lingnan came under the new dynasty. The court set up commanderies and counties along the line of Guangzhou, Xunzhou, Luozhou and Jiaozhou, and at the same time kept the practice of the Chen, appointing tribal chiefs as governors of commanderies, as county magistrates and even as ennobled leaders, entrusting them with the villages, the tribute and the levies. The fault lay in the mutual distrust between the officials and the chiefs: the officials, judged by their own record and their own profit, added to the corvee, demanded luxuries and confiscated the weapons produced in the villages, while the chiefs used their command of the mountain paths and of the villages to intercept the orders of the capital in the ravines, and the two denounced one another until the grievances had piled up in the hills. Outside provocation also played its part. More than ten years after the fall of the Chen, the surviving ministers and adherents of the Chen had taken refuge in the mountains of Lingnan, calling for the restoration of the Chen and resistance to the Sui, and they argued to the villages that the court troops were only temporarily present, tempting them to rise. Around the first year of Renshou Emperor Wen was often ill and rumours of every kind were circulating in the capital, with talk far and wide that the Sui fortune was about to end, and the mountain settlements treated such talk as an opening; the Sui levies and public works in Lingnan were also increasing, and the burden of service and of apportioned tribute fell upon the villages least able to resist, so that resentment gathered into a banner. The rising of Wang Zhongxuan at Panyu in the tenth year of Kaihuang had already shown that the hidden fire of disobedience in Lingnan was never extinguished, and the eleven years of quiet that followed were suppression rather than a cure for a structural flaw. Thus in the first year of Renshou several villages answered one another, the court could no longer manage the region with titles to chieftains and had to send troops, and Feng Ang, the governor of Guangzhou and the one commander who knew the far south, became the only leader in whom it could trust.
impact: 此役的直接影響，是隋朝在嶺南中部山區的控制從「籠統羈縻」轉為「郡縣與寨落並存的實控」，並把此後唐代嶺南治理的走向大致定了下來。事後，隋廷在所平寨地增設或升格縣治，設巡檢、置屯兵，把山口險要留給常備戍軍守禦；原有的俚族首領多保留頭銜與部分實權，改以「檢校、員外、司馬」一類名號虛領，隋廷不必年年用兵，卻也未真正削去地方勢力。這種「以夷制夷、羈縻為主、屯兵為輔」的組合，成為隋唐之際嶺南的標準做法，也直接催生了日後廣東一帶以冼氏、陳氏為代表的軍人世族政治。冼夫人至此獲致更大的權望，其家族在廣州、循州、高涼等地的影響綿延數代，日後陳元光一系在漳、泉的經營即以此為基礎；反過來，地方首領與中央之間長期共存的關係，也埋下唐代中晚期嶺南藩鎮化的隱憂。對隋朝全局而言，此役的另一重意義在於「南方可控」：隋廷得以在此後十餘年不在嶺南大舉用兵，轉而把注意力放在北方的突厥與高句麗上，直到大業年間兵制與稅制全面改革、役使急增，才重新激起包括嶺南在內的遍地反抗。換言之，601年平掉的那幾處山寨，只是隋朝崩解前一連串危機的開端；其後不到十年，楊廣即位、楊玄感起兵、各地民變接連爆發，隋室江山在全國性的反亂中崩解，嶺南的平叛成果很快被捲入這場更大的崩解之中。
impactEn: The direct effect of the campaign was that Sui control in the central mountains of Lingnan shifted from a loose chieftaincy to an effective arrangement in which commanderies and villages coexisted, and this largely set the course of government in Lingnan under the Tang. After the fighting, the court enlarged or promoted the county administrations of the pacified area, established patrols and stationed troops, and left the key passes to permanent garrisons; the existing tribal chiefs mostly kept their titles and a share of their real power, wearing nominal offices such as jianjiao, yuanwai or sima, so that the Sui no longer had to campaign every year, yet never truly dismantled the local powers. This combination, native chieftains in the lead, the state's grip held light and a garrison as the backstop, became the standard practice in Lingnan through the passage from Sui to Tang, and it directly produced the military clanship politics represented in Guangdong by the Xian and Chen families. Lady Xian here acquired still greater authority, and the influence of her family in Guangzhou, Xunzhou and Gaoliang ran on for generations; the later enterprises of the line of Chen Yuanguang in the Zhang and Quan areas rested on this foundation. At the same time, the long coexistence of local chiefs and the central government planted the seed of the fanzhen militarization of Lingnan in the middle and late Tang. For the Sui as a whole, the campaign carried a further meaning: the south was controllable. For more than a decade afterwards the court could keep its attention on the Turks and Goguryeo in the north rather than on major operations in Lingnan, until the wholesale reform of the military and tax systems in the Daye years, with the sudden increase of labour service, raised uprisings again across the empire, Lingnan among them. In short, the few mountain forts settled in 601 were only the beginning of a whole series of crises; within less than a decade the accession of Yang Guang, the revolt of Yang Xuansheng and the scattered popular risings broke the Sui apart, and the pacification of Lingnan was swept into that larger collapse.
result: 結果是隋軍平定了嶺南這一批僚人山寨，馮盎以軍功復其位，加授上柱國、廣州總管、護國公一類的勳號，而其家在廣州一帶的統治地位從此更為鞏固。起事山寨多在圍困與斷糧之下崩潰：部分首領受招撫而降，部眾被解散編為民戶或收為屯卒，一部分散入更深的山嶺，隋軍沒有展開大規模追擊，因為嶺南山地既缺水又缺糧，長驅深入只會重演糧秣耗盡的困境。隋廷隨即在新平地區改置官署、編定戶口、增設巡檢與屯戍，把戰時的臨時軍事安排轉成長期的邊防常態；同時倚重冼夫人與陳魂一系的俚族力量，令其仍舊牧領故土，成為隋朝在南疆最省力的統治方式。從戰役過程看，投石機等攻城器械確實為破寨提供了可行手段：只要能把器械運上高地、保持射界，便能摧毀寨牆、守軍與糧秣，使守方在援絕糧盡的情況下失去抵抗能力；這也說明隋唐時期南方山地攻堅的成敗，關鍵在於補給與道路，而不在器械本身的殺傷威力。史家記錄此役甚略，未載斬獲數與器械損耗，但可以確定的結果是：仁壽元年隋朝平定了嶺南中部的起事，保住了廣州至交州一線的交通與政令，統治秩序維持到隋文帝崩後、大業亂作之前；此役之後，隋朝真正的考驗才剛剛開始。
resultEn: The result was that the Sui army broke the Liao villages of Lingnan. Feng Ang was confirmed in his post and honoured with titles such as Shangzhuguo, governor of Guangzhou and protector of the state, and his family's position in the Guangzhou area grew more secure. Most of the insurgent strongholds collapsed under siege and under the cutting of their supplies: some chiefs were taken in by amnesty and their followers disbanded, enrolled as households or turned into garrison soldiers, while others scattered into the remoter mountains, and the Sui did not pursue them far, because the mountains of Lingnan lack both water and grain, and a long march in would only have reproduced the fate of exhausted supply lines. The court then reorganised the pacified districts into official administrations, registered the households, and added patrols and garrison troops, converting the emergency military arrangements of the war into a permanent frontier system; at the same time it leaned on Lady Xian and on the armed authority of the line of Chen Hun, whose people continued to shepherd their own country, and this was the cheapest form of rule the Sui possessed in the far south. The course of the fighting also shows what the onager and the other machines were worth: if they could be brought up on high ground and given a clear arc, they destroyed walls, defenders and stored grain, and left a garrison without the means of resistance once its relief and its food were cut off. It also shows that the success of a Sui or Tang siege in the southern mountains depended upon supply and roads rather than upon the killing power of any machine. The historians who record this campaign say very little about it, and no figures survive either for the losses inflicted or for the damage done to the engines, but the certain outcome was this: in the first year of Renshou the Sui settled the rising in the central mountains of Lingnan, kept the roads and the government orders running between Guangzhou and Jiaozhou, and held the administrative order in place until the death of Emperor Wen and the disorder of the Daye years. The real test of the Sui began only after that.
